elements.element: Customer owns all deliverables created for it.
elements.evidence: The Company owns all right, title and interest in the Site, including its design, look and feel, pages and materials developed by HDI for the Company.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for it.
elements.evidence: The ownership grant expressly covers “all pages and materials developed by HDI for the Company hereunder,” which encompasses the identified work product.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer Vendor's rights in those deliverables and work product.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “HDI hereby assigns such rights to the Company.”

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing IP.
elements.evidence: HDI expressly retains ownership of its “pre-existing and generally applicable hosting platform, tools and know-how.”

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: HDI grants the Company a licence to “any such HDI materials as embedded in the Site.”

elements.element: The embedded Vendor IP licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The embedded-materials licence is expressly perpetual.

elements.element: The embedded Vendor IP licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The embedded-materials licence is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: The embedded Vendor IP licence is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The embedded-materials licence is expressly royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: As between the parties, the Company owns “all right, title and interest” in all customer and user data collected through the Site.

elements.element: Deliverables, work product, Vendor IP, and Customer Data are not jointly owned.
elements.evidence: The clause allocates all rights in the Site, HDI-developed materials and Site data to the Company, while separately reserving HDI's pre-existing platform, tools and know-how to HDI. This sole-ownership allocation excludes joint ownership between the parties.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: HDI retains ownership of its “generally applicable hosting platform” and “tools.”

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic know-how.
elements.evidence: HDI expressly retains ownership of its generally applicable know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Company receives the stronger right of ownership in the Site and HDI-developed pages and materials, while embedded HDI materials are separately licensed.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The Company's ownership is not time-limited, and the licence covering embedded HDI materials is expressly perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The Company's assigned ownership is not revocable, and the licence covering embedded HDI materials is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The embedded-materials licence is expressly worldwide, and the Company's ownership of the remaining deliverable is not geographically limited.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The embedded-materials licence is expressly royalty-free, and no royalty applies to the Company-owned portions of the deliverable.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to use the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Company owns the Site and expressly receives a right to use embedded HDI materials.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Although ownership supports modification of Company-owned portions, the licence to embedded HDI materials authorizes only “use” and does not permit modification of those materials as part of the complete deliverable.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The licence to embedded HDI materials contains no sublicensing right, so the Company cannot clearly sublicense the complete deliverable with those materials included.

elements.element: The licensed rights may be exercised for Customer's business.
elements.evidence: The ownership and use rights are not restricted by purpose and therefore include use for the Company's business.

result.reason: The redline satisfies the preferred position through Company ownership, present assignment, a pre-existing-IP reservation, an embedded-IP licence with the required duration and economic terms, Company ownership of Site customer data, and mutually exclusive ownership allocations. The fallback is incomplete because the embedded HDI-materials licence permits only use, not modification or sublicensing, which prevents clear modification or sublicensing of the complete deliverable. The amendment preserves the original Site-control and service terms, but it is not strictly minimal because it adds broader fallback-oriented concepts—worldwide scope and generally applicable platform/tools/know-how—beyond what was necessary to complete the preferred position. Drafting quality is reduced by the limited “use” licence, the potentially ambiguous relationship between Company ownership of the Site and HDI ownership of embedded materials, and the broad reference to “such rights” in the assignment.
